findings.reason: The protected solution is a clear prefix-indexed backtracking implementation. Its word_length, by_prefix, square, row, prefix, and candidate names represent genuine search concepts, the recursion has minimal state, and no candidate would materially improve it.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 425 and its Python wordSquares surface. The Reference preserves the row-column definition, reuse and ordering rules, inline illustrative square, both authenticated source examples with explanations, and all five constraints from the live statement.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064776407. Apart from the required Solution method wrapper, List annotations, and app-local return types, it is structurally identical to the app-local source: both materialize all prefixes, derive the same forced next-row prefix, recurse over the same candidates, copy complete squares, and backtrack identically.

The legal 64-, 192-, and 512-word fixed-length tiers span 8x and make every first row demand an absent prefix, isolating indexed lookup from repeated dictionary scans. A fresh exact-source run passes all 11 executions at -0.00 extra growth, 1.01x the protected reference at the largest tier, and no more than 1.06x at any tier. An independently correct rescan control passes all 11 outputs but fails only the scaling verdict at +0.31 extra growth.

The Approach exactly derives each forced prefix, explains the prefix map and reusable-word backtracking, proves soundness and completeness by depth, and states the output-sensitive O(NL^2 + PL) time and O(NL^2 + L^2) auxiliary-space bounds. Its exhaustive-search alternative now uses valid mathematical notation.

The authenticated Premium statement was reviewed directly in Chrome. The modular Reference preserves the complete definition and illustrative square, both explained source examples, all five constraints, and the absence of source visuals, tables, or additional sections. source_fidelity.json is verified with live-content SHA-256 0bc8a3b5b8d6041868dcbb080cde21a55a768bbe13742b5a830c423aecca63fc and current hashes for every composed Reference section.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with their exact input arrays and source-ordered output squares; the invented one-letter example is correctly labelled a trial.

Visible cases cover word lengths 1 through 4, one input word, no available square, multiple output squares, reusable input words, and an explicit unique 1,000-word dictionary at the maximum word-count boundary.
Two-, three-, and four-row squares, self-repetition in every row, forced prefixes, absent prefixes, and outer-list order independence exercise the material construction semantics.

An independent scan oracle verified every authored and benchmark output set, every nonempty subset of the two-letter binary vocabulary, and 2,000 deterministic randomized unique dictionaries; the disjoint-prefix construction independently verified the 1,000-word boundary.
All eight correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 64-, 192-, and 512-word missing-prefix workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
